editorial.headline: The Business of Bringing Property Deals Together
editorial.standfirst: From listings to deal-making, this activity turns introductions into fees and commissions—and is nationally open to full foreign ownership, with Bali not blocked by its PMA moratorium at the recorded Large-scale risk.
editorial.body:
Real-estate intermediation is the work of making a property transaction connect: bringing clients together with sellers or service providers for the purchase, sale or rental of real estate. The consideration can be a fee or commission paid by the client, the seller, or the property-service provider. The activity is not confined to a traditional office. It may be conducted through a digital platform or through non-digital channels—face-to-face, including door to door, by telephone, by letter and similar routes. The scope also reaches real-estate listing services and may include third-party advertising-space revenue alongside intermediary income.

The record expressly places real-estate agents and independent agents inside the activity, where they provide intermediation on a fee or contract basis. It separately addresses non-exempt PPMSE and PSP based either inside Indonesia or outside it when they conduct PMSE business in Indonesia. Registration is open at every recorded scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth follows the function of the business—connecting parties and earning an agreed intermediary return—rather than limiting the work to one channel or one size of enterprise.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward: status TERBUKA with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain English, the record sets no foreign-equity ceiling below full foreign ownership for this activity at the national level. Its cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is the recorded position for the defined intermediation activity, whose revenue may arise from fees, commissions and the specified sale of advertising space to third parties.

In Bali, the record is equally clear, although it must be read through risk: its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and it is not marked as blocked. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which means the activity is not blocked by the island-wide permanent moratorium described in the record. That moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI in Bali. The practical conclusion is clean: Bali is not a registration dead end for PMA under this record; the decisive recorded fact is its Large-scale Medium-High/High risk classification.
editorial.pullQuote: At the Large scale, Bali’s Medium-High/High risk classification keeps this activity outside the island-wide PMA moratorium.
